channel.title: Paperback Galaxy
channel.description: Science fiction reviews, reading lists and recommendations.

item.title: Five hard science fiction novels for a long weekend
item.description: Real physics, big ideas, and endings that stay with you. Our picks range from a lone astronaut solving problems with chemistry to a generation ship that forgot where it was going.

item.title: Why Hyperion still works thirty-five years later
item.description: Seven pilgrims, seven stories, one terrifying destination. The frame-tale structure is the secret: every chapter is a different genre, and the whole is more than its parts.

item.title: Reading science fiction with your kids
item.description: Start with wonder, not war. A list of gentle, curious books for readers aged eight to twelve, and how to talk about the big questions they raise at the dinner table.

item.title: The Dispossessed and the art of the two-planet novel
item.description: Alternating chapters between two worlds lets a novel argue with itself. We look at how the structure carries the book's ideas about freedom and walls.

item.title: Short story roundup: September
item.description: A lighthouse keeper on a tidally locked world, a translation app that learns to lie, and a heist on a space elevator. Our favourite short fiction from the magazines this month.

item.title: Audiobooks that are better than the page
item.description: Some narrators turn a good book into a great one. Six science fiction audiobooks to make the school run or the commute fly by.

item.title: Book club guide: A Fire Upon the Deep
item.description: Discussion questions, a spoiler-free primer on the Zones of Thought, and a few notes on the pack-minded Tines for readers who find them confusing at first.
